# Changing classes and content

This page is for developers and site builders who want their own site package to install other content classes or
other demo content than the package they forked. It shows where these live, how to change them, and what to keep
stable so the installer script still finds what it expects.

7x and the Exponential Foundation strongly encourage you to share the finished package by pull request to
se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth: see [Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).

## Where classes and content live

A site package itself carries no classes and no content. It requires packages that do:

| Package (7x) | Type | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `sevenx_classes` | `contentclass` | `ezcontentclass/class-<identifier>.xml`, one file per class (33 files in the source repository) |
| `sevenx_multisite_democontent` | `contentobject` | its own classes in `ezcontentclass/`, the objects in `ezcontentobject/` (`contentobjects.xml` plus one `object-*.xml` per object), binary files in `simplefiles/` |
| `sevenx_multisite_democontent_clean` | `contentobject` | the content of the variants without demo articles |

A fork usually keeps the classes package and replaces the content package, as `cjw_multisite` does with
`cjw_multisite_democontent`. See [The demo content packages](../sevenx-multisite/the-demo-content-packages.md) and
[sevenx_classes](../sevenx-multisite/sevenx-classes.md).

## How the files are listed

Nothing in a package is installed because it is in the folder; only the install items of `package.xml` are:

```xml
<install>
  <item type="ezcontentclass" filename="class-article" sub-directory="ezcontentclass"/>
  <item type="ezcontentclass" filename="class-folder" sub-directory="ezcontentclass"/>
  <item type="ezcontentobject" filename="contentobjects" sub-directory="ezcontentobject"/>
</install>
```

`type` selects the handler (`package.ini [PackageSettings] HandlerAlias[]`, for example `ezcontentclass` =
`eZContentClassPackageHandler`), `filename` is the file without `.xml`, `sub-directory` the folder. A class file you
add needs its own `<item>`; a class file you remove needs its `<item>` removed. See
[Install items and handlers](../basics/install-items-and-handlers.md).

## Way 1: edit the files

Good for small changes: a class name, an attribute's description, a text in one object.

```bash
cd packages/acme_classes/ezcontentclass
xmllint --noout class-article.xml     # well formed after your edit
```

A class file holds the identifier, the serialized names per language, the remote ID, the attributes with their
datatype and settings, and a `<remote>` block describing where it was exported from. Keep the structure the kernel
wrote; change values, not element names.

## Way 2: build on a test site and export

Good for new classes, new attributes and new content: model it in the administration of a test installation (one
installed from your current package), then export it and copy the files into your source repository.

```bash
# classes by identifier, comma separated
php ezpm.php create acme_classes_export 'Classes export' 1.0.0 install
php ezpm.php add acme_classes_export ezcontentclass article,folder
php ezpm.php export acme_classes_export -d var/tmp

# a content subtree, without its classes
php ezpm.php create acme_content_export 'Content export' 1.0.0 install
php ezpm.php add acme_content_export ezcontentobject /content/demo --exclude-classes
php ezpm.php export acme_content_export -d var/tmp
```

The same exports are on **Setup > Packages > Create new package** (Content class export, Content object export):
[Creating packages with the wizard](creating-packages-with-the-wizard.md). Then unpack the archive and copy the
class or object files, and the `<item>` lines of its `package.xml`, into your package folder:

```bash
mkdir -p var/tmp/unpacked && tar -xzf var/tmp/acme_classes_export-*.ezpkg -C var/tmp/unpacked
```

`ezpm export` names the archive `<name>-<version>-<release>.ezpkg` (`eZPackage::exportName()`); see
[Creating packages with ezpm](creating-packages-with-ezpm.md) for the options.

> **Tip**
> Before you install a changed content package anywhere, `php ezpm.php check <package>` lists what the install would
> meet on that installation, by remote ID, and writes nothing.

## Keep remote IDs stable

Packages find things by remote ID. The class handler looks for an existing class with `eZContentClass::fetchByRemoteID()`
and asks what to do when it exists; the content install sorts objects into new, existing and conflicting by remote ID
([Look inside a package, compare it with your site](../../../features/6.0/package-compare-and-import.md)). The 7x
installer relies on fixed remote IDs as well: `mainSiteaccessHomeRemoteID()` returns "the remote id of the main site's
home node, as shipped by the demo content package".

So:

- Do not change the remote ID of an object or class the installer script refers to; search the installer for the ID
  before you touch it.
- Give new objects and classes new remote IDs (exporting from a test site does this for you).
- A fork that installs next to the 7x content should not reuse 7x remote IDs for different things.

## What is not in the packages

| Data | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Layouts, zones, blocks and layout rules (`explayouts_*` tables) | `extension/sevenx_themes_media/share/db_data.dba` and `extension/explayouts/share/`, loaded by the installer ([Layouts data and share .dba files](../sevenx-multisite/layouts-data-and-share-dba.md)) |
| Tags and star ratings of the demo content | `sevenx_themes_media`'s `share/db_data.dba`, by the same step |
| Settings, siteaccesses, roles | the installer script ([Changing the installer script](changing-the-installer-script.md)) |

A demo page that shows its blocks on the 7x site needs its layout in that extension data as well; changing only the
content package leaves the page without them.

## Before you rebuild

- [ ] Every new class or object file has its `<item>`, every removed one lost it.
- [ ] `xmllint --noout` passes for every changed XML file.
- [ ] No editor backups or other leftovers in the folders: `build.sh` packs every file except the names it excludes
      ([Rebuilding with build.sh](rebuilding-with-build-sh.md)).
- [ ] Remote IDs the installer uses are unchanged.
- [ ] The package's version and changelog are raised ([Versioning your own packages](versioning-your-own-packages.md)).
